ravi: hi folks, accepted the org invite and can clone repos, but when i try to push a branch to my feature fork i get a 403 from the UI and `git push` shows: 
```
remote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/feature/ravi-setup
To https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra.git
 ! [remote rejected] feature/ravi-setup -> feature/ravi-setup (protected branch hook declined)
error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra.git'
```
I'm on 2FA, verified work email, SSO authorized. any tips?

[devex-bot]: GitHub Push Hook Event: push rejected for ravi. Check branch protection rules and required reviewers/CI status.

jen: welcome ravi! quick things: are you pushing to the upstream repo or to a fork? we require forks for external contributors and require PRs for protected branches.

ravi: pushing to upstream because the onboarding doc said to create a feature branch on the repo. not a fork.

mike: the infra repo has a strict branch-protection policy: direct pushes to main and release/* branches are blocked; for feature/* we require at least one codeowner review and a passing CI check called `infra-ci`. if your branch name matched release/* it would be blocked. which branch name did you use?

ravi: feature/ravi-setup (copied from doc example). looks like the hook rejected it specifically as protected branch.

jen: can you run `gh auth status` and confirm you have the correct account, then `git remote -v` to show remotes? sometimes people have origin set to upstream which requires org membership perms to push.

ravi: `gh auth status` shows Authenticated to github.com as ravi-dev (user) via GitHub.com OAuth. `git remote -v` shows:
```
origin https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra.git (fetch)
origin https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra.git (push)
```
So origin is upstream.

mike: ah — if you push directly to upstream we only allow pushes from users in the "maintainers" team for certain branches. For regular contributors (everyone else) the flow is: create a fork, push branch to your fork, open a PR from your fork -> upstream. That bypasses protected-branch push restrictions. The onboarding doc should probably be clearer.

ravi: ok, i can fork and push. question: is there a quick way to change my origin to my fork?

jen: yes — after you fork on GH UI, you can run:
```
git remote set-url origin git@github.com:ravi-dev/infra.git
# then git push -u origin feature/ravi-setup
```
If you prefer HTTPS: `https://github.com/ravi-dev/infra.git`.

ravi: did the fork + push and opened a PR, but CI is failing on lint. curious why CI can't run for my PR. logs say `infra-ci` didn't trigger.

[ops-bot]: CI policy: Only PRs from forked repos require a workflow whitelist. Please comment `@infra-ci allow` on the PR to request the workflow run, or add a small commit with `[ci run]` in the message.

mike: on our org we block some Actions from running on external forks unless explicitly allowed. either comment `@infra-ci allow` like ops-bot said, or ask a maintainer to run the job.

ravi: commented `@infra-ci allow`. also added a tiny README tweak to satisfy the linter to iterate.

jen: one more FYI: if you prefer not to use forks for internal team work, ask to be added to `feature-contributors` team and we can open a temporary branch-permission for your user, but we generally prefer forks for auditability.

ravi: thanks everyone — PR is open and CI started after the allow comment. appreciate the help and the welcome :wave:
